links.outcome: Physician top-1 diagnostic accuracy with vs without LLM decision support, and over-reliance
links.effect: Top-1 accuracy rose 22.2% to 33.3% with the LLM and 23.3% to 35.0% in controls; no between-group difference (adjusted OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.45-2.19; p=0.979). Case time 94 vs 206 s.
links.quote: Top-1 accuracy increased from 22.2% to 33.3% in the intervention group and from 23.3% to 35.0% in the control group, with no between-group difference in improvement (adjusted OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.45 to 2.19; p=0.979).

links.outcome: Overconfidence and over-reliance on AI output among physicians
links.effect: Exploratory analyses showed persistent overconfidence and substantial AI over-reliance; no quantitative estimates given in the abstract.
links.quote: Exploratory analyses showed persistent overconfidence and substantial AI over-reliance.

screen.reason: Multicentre randomized controlled trial evaluating physician diagnostic performance with an LLM-based clinical decision support tool versus conventional resources using clinical vignettes.
